title: OpalByte POC econ pulse & cache/batching review
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on tokens-per-dollar and latency tradeoffs. Reviewed last week's benchmark spreadsheet, discussed caching hit rates, batching windows, and a proposed dedicated short-run for tail-latency testing. Agreed next steps: run 3 back-to-back batching profiles, share updated cost model spreadsheet, and schedule dedicated-run on private pool for 8/11.
action_items: Ethan Zhou - run three batching profiles (20ms/50ms/100ms windows) across 50k synthetic requests - due 2026-08-10
Miguel Torres - validate inference tokenization divergence on 10 dev prompts - due 2026-08-08
Sofia Patel - share updated cost model + benchmark spreadsheet link and SOC2 summary - due 2026-08-06
Priya Singh - scope network egress & VPC peering checklist for private run - due 2026-08-09
next_steps: Redwood to email benchmark spreadsheet + notes
Schedule dedicated pilot run for 2026-08-11 (2-hour slot) to measure tail latency and cache warmup
Customer to provide 2k representative prompts for caching eval
Agree on success criteria: tokens/$ >= baseline by 1.5x or 100ms median latency improvement
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. want to kick off, quick checkin, today is mostly tokens per dollar and caching notes, is that right?
[00:08] Dana Lee: Yeah that's right, thanks Sofia, we've been hitting some weird variance on the staging workload, so curious about batching and cache tuning.
[00:15] Ethan Zhou: Hi all, Ethan here. quick note, we ran the micro-bench last night with a 50ms batching window and saw about 18% improvement tokens/sec per dollar but tail latency popped a bit.
[00:26] Miguel Torres: When you say tail latency popped, what's the magnitude? are we seeing 99th go to 2s?
[00:33] Ethan Zhou: more like 99th went from 420ms to about 720ms under bursty arrivals, median still good ~120ms.
[00:40] Priya Singh: That aligns with what we saw; our user flows are bursty, so steady batching helps average cost but hurts p99.
[00:48] Sofia Patel: Okay great, so tradeoff framed. Dana, do you have the target SLO numbers?
[00:53] Dana Lee: For phase one we want median < 200ms, p95 < 600ms ideally, else we'll need a fallback. Cost is secondary but we do have a hard monthly budget cap.
[01:02] Sofia Patel: Understood. quick recap of last week's results — Ethan can you walk us through the caching numbers?
[01:08] Ethan Zhou: Sure. We instrumented prefix cache on the 7k prompt sample set. cold start hit rate was low, 10% first hour, but after warmup and with sticky keys we got to 48% hit rate which translated to roughly 26% token savings. that reduced per-token compute by about 20% in our model.
[01:22] Miguel Torres: 48% is promising. how many unique prompt prefixes are we seeing?
[01:26] Ethan Zhou: Roughly 12k unique prefixes in that set; a lot of similarity but long-tail is big. caching helps most on templated prompts.
[01:33] Dana Lee: Our product has both templated responses and free text — free text doesn't cache well, so we expect lower gains in prod.
[01:39] Sofia Patel: Makes sense. quick question on quantization — have you tried the 4-bit model variants on your side?
[01:44] Miguel Torres: We tested a 4-bit q variant locally; latency dropped about 10% but hallucination score ticked up slightly on our evals.
[01:51] Ethan Zhou: Right, quantization reduces cost but can change quality. for the POC we recommend running parallel A/B: one quantized short-run for cost, one FP16 for quality-sensitive routes.
[02:00] Olga Novik: Could that be automated in the routing? i.e., send low-risk prompts to quantized and high-risk to FP16?
[02:05] Ethan Zhou: Yes, smart routing can do that — route by confidence score or prompt tag. Redwood's runtime supports policy routing with fallbacks.
[02:13] Priya Singh: on security, we need to see SOC2 and KMS integration notes before we do anything on private.
[02:18] Sofia Patel: absolutely; I'll attach those docs after the call.
[02:21] Dana Lee: Great. back to batching — what's your recommendation on batching windows for our mix?
[02:26] Ethan Zhou: For mixed bursty workloads, we typically recommend adaptive batching: short baseline window (20ms) and a burst mode up to 100ms when queue depth increases. that gets most of the cost benefit without consistently inflating p99.
[02:39] Miguel Torres: how much does adaptive batching reduce tokens/sec/$ compared to fixed 50ms? numbers?
[02:44] Ethan Zhou: from our runs: fixed 50ms gave 18% cost improvement, adaptive got about 14% but kept p99 within our target. fixed 100ms hit 28% cost improvement but p99 rose ~3x.
[02:58] Sofia Patel: so it's a risk/reward. we can tune thresholds. also caching warmup matters — do you have suggestions for pre-warming?
[03:06] Ethan Zhou: yes, two tactics: 1) run a short pre-warm job with representative traffic to populate prefix cache, 2) leverage sticky connection patterns so repeated users benefit. pre-warm for 30-60 minutes usually helps.
[03:18] Dana Lee: we can provide 2k representative prompts for pre-warm.
[03:20] Sofia Patel: perfect, we'll run a warm-up before the dedicated run.
[03:24] Olga Novik: a question on cost reporting: can we get token, GPU, and egress broken out per route?
[03:30] Ethan Zhou: yes our console can show per-route token breakdown and cost allocation. we'll share a view and the raw spreadsheet.
[03:36] Priya Singh: egress pricing is a blind spot for us; it could swing cost for heavy responses.
[03:41] Sofia Patel: we'll add egress columns to the cost model and flag routes with large payloads.
[03:46] Dana Lee: about the dedicated short-run you mentioned earlier — what's involved?
[03:50] Ethan Zhou: it's a private pool run: we reserve capacity for 2 hours, run replay at target QPS, measure median/p95/p99 and cache warmup across time. this gives a clean tail-latency picture without noisy multitenant variance.
[04:01] Miguel Torres: any infra blockers for us? VPC peering or ip allowlists?
[04:06] Priya Singh: we'll need peering and firewall rules; also we'll want to validate KMS key access.
[04:11] Sofia Patel: noted — Priya, can you send the peering contact info after call?
[04:14] Priya Singh: yes.
[04:16] [AD-HOC NOTE] Sofia Patel: (typing) I'll attach SOC2 summary and simple peering checklist in the followup email.
[04:24] Dana Lee: quick nit, are there any redwood-maintained benchmarks for similar verticals?
[04:28] Ethan Zhou: we have a retail and support benchmarks deck; I'll link the retail-sample spreadsheet. results are usually model and prompt dependent.
[04:35] Miguel Torres: on fidelity of the benchmarking, we saw some tokenization mismatch between our token counters and Redwood's tool.
[04:41] Ethan Zhou: that sometimes happens — encoding differences, extra spaces, or truncated tokens. send us a few examples and we'll reconcile.
[04:48] Olga Novik: do we need to worry about GDPR/data residency for the cache?
[04:52] Sofia Patel: for caches we support region pinning and can disable caching for sensitive routes.
[04:58] Dana Lee: that's helpful, we'll flag PII routes.
[05:02] Miguel Torres: question: what's a realistic tokens/sec/$ target for our workload? we measured baseline ~600 tokens/sec per dollar.
[05:09] Ethan Zhou: with adaptive batching and caching you should aim for 900-1100 tokens/sec/$ depending on quant and model choice. quantized might push to 1300 but with quality caveats.
[05:19] Dana Lee: ok that gives us numbers to shoot for.
[05:22] Sofia Patel: let's map action items: Ethan will run three batching profiles, Miguel do prompt checks, Priya scope peering, I'll send docs.
[05:30] Priya Singh: timeline good. also, one more ask — can we get logs for token-level tracing during the dedicated run?
[05:36] Ethan Zhou: yes we can enable token-level traces but keep in mind retention costs; we usually keep a short window for deep dives.
[05:43] Olga Novik: will Redwood share a sample tracing config?
[05:46] Sofia Patel: yes, will attach sample tracing config and minimal retention plan.
[05:51] Dana Lee: excellent. are there any blockers from Redwood's side for the 8/11 run?
[05:56] Ethan Zhou: we need the 2k prompts, peering details, and an hour of expected QPS schedule so we can provision and reserve capacity.
[06:05] Miguel Torres: we'll get that by Monday.
[06:08] Sofia Patel: perfect. quick note — regarding competitor mention, customer asked about Anthropic earlier, said they'd looked at them for quality but cost was high.
[06:17] Dana Lee: yes, cost was an issue. Redwood's cost model looked favorable in the initial scan.
[06:23] Sofia Patel: okay. any other questions?
[06:26] Priya Singh: one question on RBAC — can we restrict who can view token traces?
[06:30] Ethan Zhou: yes RBAC supports role-based access; we can limit token-level traces to a small group.
[06:35] Dana Lee: good.
[06:37] Sofia Patel: all right, let me summarize next steps — we'll send the spreadsheet, SOC2 summary, peering checklist; Ethan runs the three profiles and shares results; customer shares 2k prompts and peering info; schedule dedicated run for 8/11. sound right?
[06:51] All: yes / yep / sounds good.
[06:56] Sofia Patel: cool, thanks everyone. we'll follow up by email with the links and the run reservation.
[07:02] [END] Note: timestamps above are approximate; conversation ran ~42 minutes.
